- requirement: "The credential helper rejects failed hides/restores and restores auth only when the origin still names the workflow's original repository (or its trusted support checkout) and its push URL agrees, not an editor-changed GitHub destination; generic GitHub extraheaders are restored scoped to the verified origin only."

  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh lines 29-54 lack GITHUB_REPOSITORY validation and pushurl/pushInsteadOf checks; lines 76-95 lack repository identity and push-routing validation; lines 45-53 record extraheader keys verbatim; lines 62-97 do not pre-validate every checkout before token injection; lines 85-92 restore extraheaders without narrowing them to the verified origin; line 102 exits 0 unconditionally; line 56 does not log reason=marker_missing.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: line 48 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Hide records extraheader keys verbatim in the editor-visible marker without checking whether the key name itself contains a credential.
  WHY: The editor process can read a credential embedded in the extraheader key name from the marker file.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 29-54 (hide path) | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Hide does not validate GITHUB_REPOSITORY before stripping credentials. It also does not inspect remote.origin.pushurl or url.*.pushInsteadOf rewrite rules before allowing the editor to run.
  WHY: An explicit pushurl or pushInsteadOf rewrite can direct editor-initiated pushes to an attacker-controlled repository while the origin URL appears legitimate.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: line 81 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore accepts any https://github.com/ origin without verifying that the owner/repository matches the expected GITHUB_REPOSITORY.
  WHY: An editor-changed origin can pass the host check and receive the workflow token.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 76-95 (restore path) | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore does not validate remote.origin.pushurl or url.*.pushInsteadOf rewrite rules before injecting GH_TOKEN.
  WHY: These settings can redirect credentialed pushes to an attacker-controlled destination.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 85-87 (extraheader case pattern) | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore accepts extraheader keys matching a broad GitHub URL pattern, including attacker-repository scopes.
  WHY: The restored authorization header can apply to requests for an attacker-controlled repository.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 62-97 (restore path, header-without-origin case) | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore can process an extraheader marker entry without first validating that checkout's origin.
  WHY: A credential can be restored into a repository whose URL was never validated.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: line 29 (`repo_git "${repo}" rev-parse --git-dir`) | severity=major | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Hide uses git -C, which discovers parent .git directories.
  WHY: It can modify a parent repository when the workspace is a nested non-checkout directory.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: line 102 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The script unconditionally exits 0, ignoring the failed flag set by restore validation failures.
  WHY: Callers proceed as if credential handling succeeded despite validation failures.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: line 59 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore exits 0 when GH_TOKEN is missing.
  WHY: The checkout remains without push credentials while the caller treats restoration as successful.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 56 and 63-64 | severity=major | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore silently exits 0 when the marker is missing or empty.
  WHY: Operators cannot distinguish a no-op restore from a skipped restore in workflow logs.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: line 23 | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Hide exits 0 instead of rejecting the operation when a stale marker from an unrestored prior hide exists.
  WHY: The helper masks a stale-marker state where credential handling is untracked.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 62-97 (restore injection loop) | severity=major | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Restore injects credentials into checkouts one at a time without pre-validating all checkouts first.
  WHY: If a later checkout fails validation, an earlier checkout has already received credentials.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: line 82 (`repo_git ... remote set-url origin ... || failed=true`) | severity=major | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore sets failed=true when remote set-url fails but still exits 0.
  WHY: Callers cannot tell restoration failed, and the stale marker persists.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: line 92 | severity=major | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore sets failed=true when an extraheader config write fails but still exits 0.
  WHY: Callers treat a partially failed credential restore as successful.
